chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"It is permissible for the sick person to recite only Al-Fatiha in the obligatory prayer, and it is permissible for the healthy person, in making up voluntary prayers during the night and day, [to recite] a single surah."
And these two narrations indicate that when choosing [to recite more than one], it is not permissible to restrict oneself to a single surah.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum recitation required for a sick person in obligatory prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the flexibility in recitation (*qira'ah*) based on the worshiper's physical state, permitting a sick person to limit themselves to Surah Al-Fatiha in obligatory prayers and a healthy person to do so in voluntary prayers. The concluding scholarly note clarifies that while single-surah recitation is valid, it is not the complete standard for a healthy individual in obligatory contexts, reflecting the Shia juristic distinction between minimum validity and recommended completeness. This highlights the pragmatic approach of Shia fiqh in accommodating ease (*rukhas*) without compromising the structural integrity of the prayer.
